en.caution: Long-term holders should watch three execution and governance risks closely. First, Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 21.9% in Q1 FY2027 from 23.0% YoY; management expects sequential improvement, so another margin miss would weaken pricing-power claims against giants like Eaton and Vertiv. Second, the October 22 CFO exit—just eight months post-IPO—and remaining multi-entity stakes held by private-equity sponsor Neos Partners create governance and share-overhang risk. Third, expanding Powertrain capacity in Tijuana, Mexico introduces cross-border tariff and ramp-execution risks while the chart stays in a steep downtrend.
cons: Adjusted EBITDA margin tightened to 21.9% in Q1 FY2027 from 23.0% a year earlier, testing pricing-power assumptions during rapid scaling.
CFO Ryan Fiedler stepped down on October 22, 2026—just eight months after the February 5 IPO—creating leadership-transition scrutiny despite an internal successor.
Shares trade 69% below their $66.00 peak and 25% below the $27.00 IPO price as analysts cut targets (Baird to $27, Oppenheimer to $40, Jefferies to $36).
Forgent remains a mid-sized North American specialist competing against scale giants Eaton, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv, with private-equity sponsor Neos Partners adding overhang risk.
en.fundamental: Forgent Power Solutions designs engineered-to-order electrical distribution gear—switchgear, transformers, power distribution units, and modular eHouses/Powerskids—with data centers contributing roughly 40%–42% of revenue, utilities ~23%, and industrial sites the remainder, primarily in North America. Its November 12, 2026 Q1 FY2027 report confirmed booming AI-power demand: revenue rose 69% YoY to $479 million, net income reached $55 million, Adjusted EBITDA hit $105 million (21.9% margin), and FY2027 guidance moved up to $2.45–$2.65 billion revenue and $587–$637 million Adjusted EBITDA. Backlog ($3.0 billion entering FY2027) fully covers FY2027 sales with nonrefundable deposits and extends into FY2028, while a 385,000-square-foot Tijuana expansion lifts capacity toward $5.8 billion. The November sell-off reflects valuation compression and high expectations rather than demand weakness, but the October 22 CFO exit, slight YoY margin dip, and intense rivalry with Eaton, Schneider Electric, Vertiv, and Powell Industries keep the moat thesis on watch.
en.headline: Forgent Power Beats Q1, Yet Valuation Reset Keeps Trend Bearish Near Lows
news: November 23, 2026: An SEC Form 4 revealed Director Gregory M. Spierkel bought 25,000 shares on November 20 at $18.48 ($462,000), following CLO Tyson Hottinger's November 16 purchase of 11,800 shares at $20.76 ($245,000). FPS rebounded 12.78% to $20.30 on November 23 on above-average volume.

November 13–23, 2026: Multiple Wall Street banks cut 12-month price targets amid AI-power multiple compression while maintaining bullish ratings, including Robert W. Baird ($38 to $27, Outperform on November 23), TD Cowen ($76 to $55), KeyBanc ($60 to $46), and Oppenheimer ($60 to $40).

November 12, 2026: Forgent reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $479 million (+69% YoY), adjusted EPS of $0.24, and Adjusted EBITDA of $105 million (21.9% margin vs. 23.0% YoY), while raising FY2027 revenue guidance to $2.45–$2.65 billion. Shares still fell roughly 10% on November 12 and slid to $18.00 by November 20 as guidance lagged lofty expectations.

October 22, 2026: Forgent disclosed in SEC Form 8-K filings that CFO Ryan Fiedler stepped down effective October 21 to spend time with family and move into an advisory role, with no accounting disagreements. EVP of Finance Amy Ard, a founding team member, was appointed CFO.
en.opportunity: The stark disconnect between Forgent's collapsing share price—down 69% from its $66.00 peak to roughly a $5.8 billion market cap—and its accelerating fundamentals is notable for patient AI-infrastructure investors. Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.45–$2.65 billion is 100% covered by a backlog reinforced with nonrefundable deposits, with roughly 40% stretching into FY2028 as hyperscalers and AI labs lock in custom powertrains. Once the Tijuana expansion opens in Q4 FY2027, total annual revenue capacity reaches ~$5.8 billion, and open-market insider purchases around $18.48–$20.76 signal management confidence if margins expand on schedule.
en.opportunityCheck: The page's AI-opportunity sub-scores look broadly sensible, rightly reflecting rapid data-center electrical demand, Forgent's mid-tier competitive standing against Eaton and Vertiv, and modest product optionality. However, AI revenue exposure merits a slight upward revision: Q1 FY2027 orders nearly doubled year-over-year, driven heavily by hyperscalers and frontier AI labs whose multi-year bookings now fill FY2027 guidance and extend into FY2028. Conversely, bottleneck and pricing power should be kept conservative or nudged slightly lower until Forgent proves its Q1 Adjusted EBITDA margin dip to 21.9% reverses as new capacity ramps.
pros: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue surged 69% YoY to $479 million on November 12, 2026, with adjusted EPS of $0.24 topping the ~$0.20 estimate.
Multi-year backlog backed by nonrefundable deposits covers 100% of raised FY2027 revenue guidance ($2.45–$2.65 billion), with ~40% extending into FY2028.
A $35 million, 385,000-square-foot Tijuana Powertrain expansion due in Q4 FY2027 lifts total annual revenue capacity by ~$800 million to ~$5.8 billion.
Insiders bought stock on the dip, including Director Gregory Spierkel's $462,000 purchase at $18.48 on November 20 and CLO Tyson Hottinger's $245,000 buy on November 16.
risks: Margin pressure: Q1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 21.9% from 23.0% YoY; failure to expand sequentially would challenge pricing power.
Competitive scale: Competes directly with much larger global electrical leaders Eaton, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv once industry lead times normalize.
Private-equity overhang: Sponsor Neos Partners retains large ownership stakes after May and July 2026 secondary offerings, risking future share supply.
Hyperscaler capex cyclicality: Roughly 40%–42% of revenue comes from North American data centers, exposing orders to any AI spending pause.
Execution and cross-border risk: October 2026 CFO transition and a 385,000-sq-ft Tijuana, Mexico plant expansion carry operational and U.S.-Mexico tariff exposure.
en.summary: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS), an engineered-to-order switchgear, transformer, and modular eHouse maker, delivered a strong fiscal Q1 2027 on November 12, 2026, with revenue jumping 69% year-over-year to $479 million and full-year guidance raised to $2.45–$2.65 billion. Yet shares plunged toward their $17.67 low on lofty expectations, a slight Adjusted EBITDA margin dip to 21.9%, an October 22 CFO transition, and widespread analyst target cuts. A 12.78% bounce to $20.30 on November 23—after insider share purchases—eases selling pressure, but the post-IPO downtrend stays intact.
en.technical: As a recent listing that debuted on February 5, 2026 (202 trading days of history), FPS lacks multi-year technical context, so long-term levels carry lower statistical weight. Even so, the prevailing structure is decisively bearish. On November 23, 2026, FPS jumped 12.78% to USD 20.30, yet remains well beneath all three Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs—trend averages weighting recent prices): EMA 50 (USD 28.00), EMA 100 (USD 31.76), and EMA 200 (USD 37.08), stacked in bearish order. Momentum shows only early stabilization: MACD (12/26/9—a trend-momentum gauge) sits deeply negative at -2.84, just above its -2.97 signal line for a slight +0.13 histogram, while RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge; below 30 is oversold) recovered to 41.05, still under the 50 neutral line. Within Bollinger Bands (20/2—a volatility channel around the 20-day mean), price sits in the lower half between the USD 16.56 lower band and USD 22.89 middle band, and just 5.4% above its USD 17.67 52-week low versus a USD 66.00 high. Volume of 13.45 million shares—23% above the 10.92 million 20-day average—supports the bounce, leaving USD 17.67 as key support and USD 22.89 then USD 28.00 as resistance.

th.summary: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) ผู้ผลิต switchgear, หม้อแปลง และ eHouse สำหรับดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์ รายงานงบไตรมาส 1 ปีบัญชี 2027 เมื่อ 12 พ.ย. 2026 แข็งแกร่ง รายได้พุ่ง 69% YoY สู่ $479 ล้าน พร้อมปรับเพิ่มเป้ารายได้ทั้งปีเป็น $2.45–$2.65 พันล้าน ทว่าหุ้นกลับร่วงใกล้จุดต่ำสุด $17.67 จากความคาดหวังที่สูงมาก, Adjusted EBITDA margin อ่อนตัวเล็กน้อยสู่ 21.9%, การเปลี่ยน CFO เมื่อ 22 ต.ค. และนักวิเคราะห์หั่นเป้าราคา แม้ดีดกลับ 12.78% สู่ $20.30 เมื่อ 23 พ.ย. หลังผู้บริหารเข้าซื้อหุ้น แต่โครงสร้างขาลงหลัง IPO ยังไม่เปลี่ยน
th.technical: เนื่องจาก FPS เพิ่งเข้าตลาดเมื่อ 5 ก.พ. 2026 (มีข้อมูลซื้อขาย 202 วัน) ประวัติกราฟระยะยาวยังสั้น ทำให้สัญญาณระยะยาวมีน้ำหนักจำกัด อย่างไรก็ตาม โครงสร้างปัจจุบันยังเป็นขาลงชัดเจน แม้ราคาวันที่ 23 พ.ย. 2026 ดีดแรง 12.78% มาปิดที่ USD 20.30 แต่ยังต่ำกว่าเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยเคลื่อนที่ EMA (เส้นค่าเฉลี่ยที่ให้น้ำหนักราคาล่าสุดมากกว่า) ทั้ง 3 เส้นคือ EMA 50 (USD 28.00), EMA 100 (USD 31.76) และ EMA 200 (USD 37.08) ซึ่งเรียงตัวแบบขาลง ด้านโมเมนตัมเพิ่งเริ่มชะลอการลง: MACD 12/26/9 (ตัววัดทิศทางและแรงส่ง) ยังติดลบที่ -2.84 แต่ขยับเหนือเส้น signal (-2.97) เล็กน้อยจนฮิสโตแกรมเป็น +0.13 ส่วน RSI 14 (มาตรวัดแรงซื้อขาย 0–100; ต่ำกว่า 30 คือขายมากเกินไป) ฟื้นสู่ 41.05 แต่ยังต่ำกว่าเส้นกลาง 50 ในกรอบ Bollinger Bands 20/2 (กรอบความผันผวนรอบค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วัน) ราคาอยู่ครึ่งล่างระหว่างกรอบล่าง USD 16.56 กับเส้นกลาง USD 22.89 และอยู่สูงกว่าจุดต่ำสุด 52 สัปดาห์ที่ USD 17.67 เพียง 5.4% (เทียบจุดสูงสุด USD 66.00) วอลุ่ม 13.45 ล้านหุ้นสูงกว่าค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วัน (10.92 ล้านหุ้น) ราว 23% ช่วยหนุนการรีบาวด์ โดยมีแนวรับสำคัญที่ USD 17.67 และแนวต้านที่ USD 22.89 ถัดไปคือ USD 28.00
